visits.note:
CC: sore throat x2 days.
HPI: 24F with sore throat, painful swallowing, subjective fever. No cough. No sick contacts reported.
Exam: T 100.9 F. Tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes. Lungs clear.
Tests: rapid strep antigen ordered and reviewed, POSITIVE.
Assessment: streptococcal pharyngitis.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg twice daily x10 days. Salt water gargles, return if unable to swallow fluids.

CC: sore throat.
HPI: 67M with 3 days of sore throat and fever to 101 at home. No cough, no rash.
Exam: T 100.4 F. Erythematous pharynx with exudate. Anterior cervical adenopathy.
Tests: rapid strep antigen ordered and reviewed, POSITIVE.
Assessment: strep pharyngitis.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days. Fluids, acetaminophen as needed.

CC: sore throat and fever.
HPI: 31M, 2 days of throat pain, fever, no cough.
Exam: T 101.2 F, tonsillar swelling with exudate.
Tests: rapid strep ordered and reviewed, POSITIVE.
Assessment: pharyngitis, strep positive.
Plan: penicillin VK 500 mg BID x10 days.

CC: throat pain.
HPI: 71F with sore throat for 2 days, low appetite, no cough.
Exam: T 100.6 F. Exudative tonsils, tender nodes.
Tests: rapid strep ordered and reviewed, POSITIVE.
Assessment: streptococcal pharyngitis.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days, hydration.

CC: congestion and cough x4 days.
HPI: 29F with runny nose, mild dry cough, no fever, no shortness of breath.
Exam: afebrile, clear rhinorrhea, lungs clear, normal work of breathing.
Assessment: viral upper respiratory infection.
Plan: supportive care, over-the-counter guaifenesin and saline spray, return if fever or symptoms past 10 days.

CC: burning with urination.
HPI: 35F, 2 days of dysuria and frequency. No fever, no flank pain, not pregnant.
Exam: afebrile, no CVA tenderness, mild suprapubic tenderness.
Tests: urine dipstick ordered and reviewed, positive leukocytes and nitrites.
Assessment: uncomplicated urinary tract infection.
Plan: nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days, fluids, return if fever or back pain.

CC: cough, fever, chills.
HPI: 52M with 5 days of productive cough, fever to 102.4, chills, body aches and fatigue. Seen at an outside
emergency department 3 weeks ago for chest wall pain; I reviewed that visit's discharge summary today.
Exam: T 102.1 F, HR 104, SpO2 94% on room air. Crackles right lower lobe.
Orders: chest x-ray 2 views and CBC ordered; results reviewed with the patient.
Assessment: community-acquired pneumonia, acute illness with systemic symptoms.
Plan: azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2-5. Strict return precautions for worsening breathing.

CC: wheezing.
HPI: 41F with known moderate persistent asthma, 3 days of worsening wheeze and night cough after a cold,
using albuterol every 3 hours.
Exam: expiratory wheeze bilaterally, speaks full sentences, SpO2 96%.
Assessment: moderate persistent asthma with acute exacerbation.
Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily x5 days, albuterol refill, asthma action plan reviewed, follow up with PCP in 1 week.

CC: chest pressure.
HPI: 64M with 1 hour of substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm with sweating. History of hypertension and smoking.
Exam: diaphoretic, BP 168/96, HR 98.
ECG: performed in clinic, nonspecific ST changes.
Assessment: chest pain, possible acute coronary syndrome, a threat to bodily function.
Plan: aspirin given, EMS called, transferred to the emergency department for admission evaluation.

CC: headache.
HPI: 38F with band-like headache since this morning after a long work week. No fever, no vision change,
no weakness, no worst-headache-of-life features. Similar headaches in the past.
Exam: normal neuro exam, mild trapezius tenderness.
Assessment: tension-type headache.
Plan: ibuprofen over the counter, hydration, sleep, return if new neurologic symptoms.

CC: low back pain.
HPI: 46M with low back pain after lifting boxes yesterday, no leg weakness, no numbness, no bladder changes.
Exam: paraspinal tenderness, negative straight leg raise, normal strength.
Assessment: acute low back strain.
Plan: heat, over-the-counter naproxen, activity as tolerated, home exercises given.
Total time on the date of the encounter: 22 minutes.

CC: dizziness.
HPI: 58F with room-spinning dizziness when rolling over in bed for 2 days. No hearing loss, no weakness.
Exam: positive Dix-Hallpike on the right, normal neuro exam.
Assessment: dizziness, likely benign positional vertigo.
Plan: canalith repositioning taught, meclizine 25 mg as needed, fall precautions, counseling on red flags.
Total time on the date of the encounter: 35 minutes, including counseling and documentation.

CC: cut hand.
HPI: 27M cut his right palm on a kitchen knife 1 hour ago. Tetanus up to date. No numbness.
Exam: 3.0 cm linear laceration of the right palm, no tendon exposure, full strength and sensation.
Procedure: irrigated, lidocaine 1% local, simple repair with 5 sutures, 3.0 cm.
Assessment: laceration of the right hand.
Plan: wound care, suture removal in 10-14 days.

CC: cut forearm; also sinus pain.
HPI: 33F cut her left forearm on a shelf edge today. Separately, 12 days of facial pressure, purulent
nasal discharge and worsening congestion after initial improvement.
Exam: 2.0 cm superficial laceration left forearm. Maxillary sinus tenderness, purulent drainage.
Procedure: simple repair of 2.0 cm laceration with 3 sutures.
Assessment: 1) forearm laceration, repaired. 2) acute bacterial sinusitis.
Plan: wound care, suture removal in 7-10 days. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg BID x7 days for sinusitis.

CC: cut thumb; also red eye.
HPI: 44M cut his left thumb on sheet metal at home. Separately, right eye redness with crusting since yesterday.
Exam: 1.5 cm superficial laceration left thumb. Right conjunctival injection with mucopurulent discharge, normal vision.
Procedure: simple repair with 2 sutures.
Assessment: 1) thumb laceration, repaired. 2) acute bacterial conjunctivitis, right eye.
Plan: wound care, suture removal in 10 days. Polymyxin-trimethoprim drops 4 times daily x7 days.

CC: ear pain.
HPI: 19F with left ear pain x2 days after a cold.
Exam: bulging erythematous left tympanic membrane.
Assessment: acute otitis media, left.
Plan: amoxicillin 875 mg BID x10 days.

CC: sore throat and congestion.
HPI: 50M with 3 days of scratchy throat and nasal congestion, no fever.
Exam: mild pharyngeal erythema, no exudate, lungs clear.
Assessment: viral upper respiratory infection.
Plan: over-the-counter lozenges and fluids.

CC: twisted ankle; also a cold.
HPI: 22M rolled his right ankle playing basketball today, can bear weight with pain. Also 3 days of runny nose.
Exam: lateral right ankle swelling and tenderness over the ATFL, no bony tenderness at the malleolus tip.
X-ray: right ankle 3 views ordered and reviewed, no fracture.
Assessment: 1) right ankle sprain. 2) viral URI.
Plan: ankle brace, RICE, ibuprofen over the counter, supportive care for URI.

CC: abdominal pain.
HPI: 26F with 12 hours of pain that started near the navel and moved to the right lower abdomen, nausea, no vomiting.
I reviewed her outside urgent care note from last week, which documented a negative pregnancy test.
Exam: T 99.9 F, RLQ tenderness with guarding, positive Rovsing sign.
Orders: CBC and urinalysis ordered and reviewed, WBC 13.8.
Assessment: right lower quadrant pain, undiagnosed new problem with uncertain prognosis, appendicitis not excluded.
Plan: sent to the emergency department for CT and surgical evaluation; decision made to escalate care.

CC: bug bite.
HPI: 12M with an itchy bump on the left shin after camping. No fever, no spreading redness.
Exam: 1 cm raised papule, no warmth, no drainage.
Assessment: insect bite of the left lower leg, minor.
Plan: over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, cool compress, return if spreading redness.

CC: red eye.
HPI: 8F with left eye redness and morning crusting x1 day. Mother provides the history.
Exam: left conjunctival injection with mucopurulent discharge, normal acuity.
Assessment: acute bacterial conjunctivitis, left eye.
Plan: polymyxin-trimethoprim drops 4 times daily x7 days, school note given.

CC: itchy rash.
HPI: 36M with an itchy linear rash on both forearms 2 days after clearing brush.
Exam: linear vesicular streaks on both forearms, no facial involvement, no signs of infection.
Assessment: allergic contact dermatitis due to plants.
Plan: triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily x14 days, oral antihistamine over the counter.

CC: cough and congestion.
HPI: 69F with 2 days of cough, congestion and sore throat. No fever, no shortness of breath.
Exam: afebrile, SpO2 97%, lungs clear.
Tests: COVID-19 antigen ordered and reviewed, negative.
Assessment: viral upper respiratory infection.
Plan: over-the-counter dextromethorphan, fluids, rest, return if breathing worsens.

CC: fever and body aches.
HPI: 70M with sudden fever to 101.8, chills, myalgias, headache and dry cough since yesterday.
Exam: T 101.6 F, HR 102, SpO2 95%, lungs clear.
Tests: influenza antigen and COVID-19 antigen ordered and reviewed; influenza A POSITIVE, COVID negative.
Assessment: influenza A, acute illness with systemic symptoms, higher risk due to age.
Plan: oseltamivir 75 mg BID x5 days, fluids, return precautions for breathing difficulty.

CC: cough and congestion.
HPI: 28F with 1 day of mild cough, congestion and scratchy throat. Afebrile at home. Roommate has the flu.
Exam: afebrile, mild nasal congestion, lungs clear.
Tests: influenza antigen ordered and reviewed, influenza A POSITIVE.
Assessment: influenza A, mild.
Plan: oseltamivir 75 mg BID x5 days given known exposure and onset within 48 hours, fluids.

CC: back pain.
HPI: 39M strained his lower back moving furniture yesterday. No radiation, no numbness, no bladder or bowel changes.
Exam: lumbar paraspinal spasm and tenderness, negative straight leg raise, normal strength and reflexes.
Assessment: strain of lower back muscles, acute, uncomplicated.
Plan: cyclobenzaprine 10 mg at night x7 days, ibuprofen 800 mg TID with food x7 days, heat, gentle activity.

CC: headache, high home blood pressure readings.
HPI: 61F with known hypertension on lisinopril, home readings 170s-180s/100s this week, mild headache.
No chest pain, no vision change, no weakness. I reviewed her PCP's notes from her last two visits.
Exam: BP 182/104 repeated 178/102, normal neuro exam, no edema.
Orders: basic metabolic panel ordered and reviewed, creatinine at baseline.
Assessment: essential hypertension, poorly controlled (chronic illness with progression); headache.
Plan: add amlodipine 5 mg daily, continue lisinopril, recheck BP with PCP in 1 week, ED precautions.

CC: dog bite.
HPI: 45F bitten on the back of the right hand by her neighbor's dog 3 hours ago. Dog vaccinated.
Exam: two puncture wounds over the 3rd metacarpal with surrounding swelling; tendon function intact,
full range of motion, sensation intact. Wound left open given bite risk.
Assessment: dog bite puncture wounds of the right hand, an acute complicated injury given infection risk
and closeness to the extensor tendon.
Plan: irrigation, amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg BID x5 days as prophylaxis, wound check in 48 hours.

CC: sore throat.
HPI: 74M with 2 days of sore throat and fever.
Exam: exudative pharyngitis, tender anterior nodes.
Tests: rapid strep ordered and reviewed, POSITIVE.
Assessment: strep pharyngitis.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg BID x10 days.

CC: bite on the arm.
HPI: 30F with an itchy bump on the left forearm since yesterday. No fever, no spreading redness.
Exam: small raised papule, no warmth or drainage.
Assessment: insect bite of the left forearm, minor.
Plan: over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and an oral antihistamine as needed.
